insights.insight: The protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at ~$0.10 per receipt (148 sats) against ad tech CPA rates of $5–$150 for probabilistic attribution — a 50–200x cost delta that is structural, not a promotional rate.

A single 4-hour window added $55,679.99 in GMV across only 54 receipts, implying an average ticket of ~$1,031 — well above protocol norms — concentrated in retail/department stores, which jumped from a ~$78 to ~$185 average ticket in the 14-day window.

insights.topic: Retail category breadth as targeting surface
insights.insight: Verified receipts now span grocery, restaurants, gas/convenience, pharmacy (CVS), big-box, specialty, warehouse clubs, automotive, and peer-to-peer resale — the category stack covers enough of the purchase funnel to support audience segmentation across most CPG and retail verticals.

insights.topic: Pharmacy and resale as emerging verified channels
insights.insight: CVS Pharmacy holds 31 receipts in the 14-day window and Depop holds 14, confirming that pharmacy and peer-to-peer resale are now structurally present in the receipt mix — not transient — which opens verified targeting for health/beauty and secondhand-market brands.

insights.topic: Growth regime shift: sustainable, not compounding
insights.insight: Velocity sits at 1.091x (network growing faster than its trailing baseline) but acceleration has dropped below 1.0x for the first time, signaling a transition from anomalous compounding growth to normalized, sustainable throughput — a more reliable baseline for audience size projections.

191 receipts in a 14-day window carry an ~$144 average ticket but remain categorically unresolved; resolving this bucket would materially shift the retail-vs-services split and could surface a high-value segment currently invisible to brand planners.
